notes: Connected OSM course candidate. The selected loop is the longest simple source-node cycle after explicit exclusions; its association with a named circuit configuration requires review.
Source way order and shared node IDs are retained. No nearby endpoints are joined and no reference boundaries are read.
Some source ways lack one-way direction tags. Travel direction is provisional.

sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 68 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the midpoint of corresponding border stations, not an official length measurement. There is no saved GPS start gate; the simulation begins at the first trace coordinate. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.

refinement.note: Fifty positions measured on the pinned NAIP image correct the straight-side asphalt seams, narrowed bends and false pit-side detections. The southern raceway is separated from the parallel pit/apron strip using its visible pavement transitions. Four preserved seam endpoints retain closure. Offsets interpolate through the original cross-section frames between measured positions, including shared-pavement junctions; these are unverified estimates, not a continuous edge survey or curb extraction. No assumed constant road width is supplied.

borderInference.note: Automatically inferred from RGB differences along cross-sections of the existing trace. Evidence scores are not calibrated positional confidence. Borders are estimates and have not been formally verified; shadows, trees, aprons, paint and imagery age can move the detected edge. Imagery resolution is not survey accuracy. Sparse edge anchors measured on the pinned image correct the documented sections. Evidence scores describe the original automatic proposal, not the corrected borders. The seed and final border hashes and correction recipe are retained.
